newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell off more than 62 pct of ginnery.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell off more than 62 pct of ginnery.

text.p: The Egyptian state will sell 62.65 percent of Arab Cotton Ginning after demand for the firm exceeded slightly the stake it had offered, an official at the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) said on Tuesday.

Mahmoud el-Shanawani, general manager of the CMA's information department, told Reuters the holding company for Cotton and International Trade sold a total 52.65 percent of the ginnery to private investors. It had offered them 51 percent.
The firm's workers were also allocated the traditional 10 percent or 224,000 shares.
Shanawani said individuals bought 947,135 shares, or 42.25 percent and mutual funds and investment institutions bought an additional 10.4 percent.
The shares were sold at 27 pounds each and the ginnery will pay a 2.00 pound dividend for the 1995/6 financial year compared to 2.65 for the previous year.
The holding company said Arab Cotton Ginning made net after-tax profits of 6.620 million pounds in the financial year ending June 30 1996, compared with 11.146 million in the previous year.
It forecast the company's net after-tax profits would rise to 6.853 million in the current financial year and to 7.341 million in the year 1997/8.
